newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes mixed, underpinned late by corn.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes mixed, underpinned late by corn.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with the market buoyed in late dealings by a rally in corn futures, especially in the December corn contract, traders said.
The market was weakened early on follow through from the late break in the market Wednesday plus further evidence of strong competition for export business.

An European Union grain official said Thursday the EU remains a seller of wheat on the world market but volumes between now and the end of the season will depend strictly on bids at its weekly tender.
But the market was underpinned by USDA export data.
USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended March 6 totalled 355,400 tonnes, above expectations for 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes.
Nearby March was pressured by long liquidation. March is slated to expire Wednesday and traders were getting out of that contract.
Wheat closed three cents lower to four cents higher, with March down two at $3.74. New crop July was up 1/4 cent at $3.68-1/4.

Technicians early Thursday cited first resistance in the March at $3.80-1/2 and second resistance at $3.87-1/2. The session high for March was $3.76. First support was at $3.73-1/2 and second support was at $3.66-1/2. The session low was $3.69.

The four- and 20-day moving averages were giving off bullish signals early Thursday. The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) in the March closed at 53 percent. The market generally considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 17,000 contracts, below the 33,171 traded Wednesday.
In wheat options, Tenco Inc sold 200 December $4.30 calls at 11 to 12 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,000 contracts, below the 11,377 traded Wednesday.
